identity.name: Democratic Republic of Vietnam

land.text: Vietnam north of the 16th parallel, where Chinese Nationalist forces disarmed the Japanese and, after the Ho-Sainteny Agreement of 6 March 1946, French forces replaced them

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws French Indochina over all of Vietnam to 1955 and starts the DRV in 1956; the state declared independence on 2 September 1945.

land.text: all of Vietnam: 'officially reunited on 2 July 1976 as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam'

successors.note: The Democratic Republic and the Republic of South Vietnam (PRG) 'constitutionally merged' (PRG page); Cliopatria's Socialist Republic row starts on 1 January 1976, six months early.

capitals.name: Hanoi
capitals.note: The page names Hanoi as the capital; Chinese Nationalist troops evacuated it in June 1946.

capitals.name: Tuyên Quang province (mountain base)
capitals.note: The page: the government operated 'from the mountainous areas, mostly in Tuyên Quang province, between 1947 and October 1954'; the town of Tuyên Quang stands for the base.

capitals.name: Hanoi
capitals.note: Capital again from October 1954 and of the reunified country in July 1976.

rulers.title: President

correction.text: Vietnam north of the 16th parallel, the zone in which Chinese Nationalist forces disarmed the Japanese in 1945 and where 'the Ho-Sainteny Agreement of 6 March 1946 let French forces replace the Chinese'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the DRV 'declared independence on 2 September 1945' and the infobox gives 331,212 km2 for 1945 (its claim to all Vietnam), but the page shows the real hold north of the 16th parallel and Chinese troops in the north until the last embarked at Haiphong on 15 June 1946, French forces replacing them. The zone is 596 grid cells against 551 for the Cliopatria 1956 shape (the strip between the 16th and 17th parallels).

correction.text: the mountain base, 'mostly in Tuyên Quang province', from which the government operated between 1947 and October 1954

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after 19 December 1946 'the government operated from the mountainous areas, mostly in Tuyên Quang province' while 'the Viet Minh controlled most rural areas during the guerrilla war'. The base is the solid shape; the rural fighting zone is the contest event (French Indochina holds the towns).

correction.text: the northern zone of the Geneva Accords of 21 July 1954, which 'provisionally divided the country into a northern zone and a southern zone along the 17th parallel'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Cliopatria 1956 shape (157,593 km2) applies from the Geneva Accords; the infobox gives 157,880 km2 for 1955 and 1968 (ratio 1.00). The page does not date the takeover of Hanoi (October 1954) or Haiphong (May 1955).

157,593 km2 for 1956-1966 against the infobox 157,880 km2 for 1955 and 1968 (ratio 1.00): the territory north of the 17th parallel. The page says the Geneva Accords divided the country 'along the 17th parallel' and does not mention the Ben Hai River or the DMZ.
158,088 km2 for 1967-1972: 495 km2 more than the 1956 shape, no border change on the page (infobox 157,880 km2 for 1968, ratio 1.00); treated as grid noise.

correction.text: the DRV proper north of the 17th parallel, 1973-1975; the border zones that Cliopatria adds in 1973 are occupations (events), not DRV territory

keyframe_review.note: 186,286 km2 for 1973-1975, unverified beyond the PRG's capital at Cam Lo: the shape is the 1972 shape plus about 28,200 km2 (51 cells in Vietnam, 37 in Laos, 14 in Cambodia) that Cliopatria also removes from the Republic of Vietnam (10,875 km2 of its 1966 shape), the Kingdom of Laos (the Ho Chi Minh Trail strip, cut in 1967) and Cambodia (the north-east). These are zones held by the Provisional Revolutionary Government and the PAVN, so they are carried as hatched occupations: the PRG page says it was formed on 8 June 1969 'by the Democratic Republic of Vietnam', 'signed the 1973 Paris Peace Treaty as an independent entity, separate from both South Vietnam and North Vietnam' and had its capital at Cam Lo 1973-1975; its infobox area is 173,809 km2 for 1975. A PRG dossier should take the Vietnamese zone. Reviewer fix: the Laotian zones are now carried by three occupation events, the 1967 strip, Attapu (1970-05) and the Bolaven Plateau (1971), the last two mirrored from kingdom-of-laos.

correction.text: all of Vietnam until the formal reunification of 2 July 1976

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the war 'ended on 30 April 1975' and the country was 'officially reunited on 2 July 1976 as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam'; Cliopatria's DRV row ends in 1975 and its Socialist Republic row begins in January 1976, so the DRV carries the whole country in 1976 until 2 July. The Socialist Republic dossier should start in July 1976 or the compiler hand over in the middle of 1976.

region.text: the north, where 'Chinese Nationalist forces arrived ... to disarm the Japanese'

ledger.note: August 1945: the August Revolution page says 'On 20 August, Chiang Kai-shek gave orders for the Chinese First Front Army, under the command of General Lu Han' and that 'General Lu Han's 200,000 Chinese soldiers occupied north Vietnam starting August 1945'; 'The Chinese left only in April-June 1946'. The page gives no arrival day, so the month is the page's 'starting August 1945' and the region (north of the 16th parallel) is the researcher's reading; the North Vietnam page is silent on the arrival. The occupation opens a month before the DRV's founding on 2 September 1945.

region.text: Vietnam north of the 16th parallel, the DRV's real hold after the Chinese took the surrender of the Japanese

ledger.note: 1945: Hồ Chí Minh declares the independence of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam at Hanoi (2 September). The page 'declared independence on 2 September 1945' and links Hanoi as capital without naming the place of the proclamation; the infobox area for 1945 (331,212 km2) is the claim to the whole of Vietnam.

region.text: the north: 'In June, Chinese Nationalist troops evacuated Hanoi, and on 15 June, the last detachments embarked at Haiphong'

ledger.note: 1946: the Chinese leave (June; the last detachments embark at Haiphong on 15 June). The Ho-Sainteny Agreement of 6 March 1946 had let French forces replace them north of the 16th parallel.

region.text: all Vietnam: 'The Viet Minh controlled most rural areas during the guerrilla war' while the French held the towns

ledger.note: 1946: the First Indochina War begins (19 December, infobox). The French hold the urban areas and the Viet Minh 'most rural areas'; the government retires to the mountains of Tuyên Quang.

region.text: all Vietnam, fought over in the First Indochina War

ledger.note: 1954: the Geneva Accords (21 July; the footnoted agreement is dated 20 July) end the war.

region.text: the northern zone: 'provisionally divided the country into a northern zone and a southern zone along the 17th parallel'

ledger.note: 1954: the DRV is confirmed north of the 17th parallel (Geneva Accords, 21 July). The infobox gives 'sovereign (1954-1976)'. The page does not date the takeover of Hanoi (October 1954) or of Haiphong (May 1955); the region is the Cliopatria 1956 shape.

region.text: the south-eastern border strip (Xekong, Attapu, eastern Savannakhet, Saravan; about 10,600 km2) that Cliopatria cuts from the Kingdom's shape in 1967: 'North Vietnam invaded and occupied parts of Laos as a supply route'

ledger.note: 1967: the Ho Chi Minh Trail strip of south-eastern Laos. The page says only that the trail 'carried North Vietnamese and Viet Cong forces and supplies' and that the DRV aided the Pathet Lao: page silent on territory and date; the year is Cliopatria's cut from the Kingdom of Laos. Reviewer follow-up, checked on the Ho Chi Minh trail and Laotian Civil War pages: the PAVN and Pathet Lao 'seized the transportation hub at Tchepone, on Laotian Route 9' in May 1958, 'Construction for the network began following the North Vietnamese invasion of Laos in July 1959' (Group 559 set up on 15 May 1959 per the Laotian page, in September 1959 per the trail page), the Laotian page has the North Vietnamese Army and Pathet Lao 'occupying the east of the country' in 1958 and 1959, and Attapeu and Salavan fall 'during 1970'. Neither page dates the occupation of the strip as a whole (Xekong and Savannakhet are undated), so 1967 stays Cliopatria's year at confidence 1; the occupation of eastern Laos is earlier (1958-59) and the Laotian events of 1970-71 are now separate events. kingdom-of-laos /ledger/5 carries the same date and should move with it.

region.text: the north-east of Cambodia seized by the PAVN offensive from 29 March 1970 ('all five of Cambodia's northeastern provinces' by April; the four provinces drawn are the researcher's reading)

ledger.note: 1970: the PAVN takes the Cambodian north-east. Its offensive from 29 March 1970 was 'seizing large portions of the eastern and northeastern parts of the country'; by April it had 'taken all five of Cambodia's northeastern provinces' and 'turned the newly won territories over to local insurgents'. The Khmer Rouge is the Cambodian dossier's counterpart.

region.text: Attapeu, seized on 1 May 1970 by PAVN units joined with the Pathet Lao

ledger.note: 1 May 1970: 'elements of SVN PAVN units (28th and 24A regiments) joined with North Vietnamese Army and Pathet Lao to seize Attapeu'; the Ho Chi Minh trail page also has Attapeu and Salavan 'seized by the PAVN during 1970'. Reviewer fix: mirrors kingdom-of-laos /ledger/6, which already carries this occupation; only 11 of Attapu's 29 cells lie in the 1967 strip of /ledger/6.

region.text: the Bolaven Plateau, captured in 1971 by Pathet Lao and PAVN forces; the 60 km circle is the researcher's reading

ledger.note: 1971: the Pathet Lao and PAVN 'captured the Bolaven Plateau' (Laotian Civil War page, placed in 1971); the Ho Chi Minh trail page has 'During 1971 PAVN took Paksong and advanced to Pakse'. The 60 km circle at 106.3 E 15.1 N is the researcher's reading of the plateau, as in kingdom-of-laos /ledger/7, which this mirrors; none of its cells lie in the 1967 strip.

region.text: the north-east of Cambodia seized by the PAVN offensive from 29 March 1970 ('all five of Cambodia's northeastern provinces' by April; the four provinces drawn are the researcher's reading)

ledger.note: 1972: the PAVN withdraws from the north-east. North Vietnamese forces 'gradually and deliberately scaled back their presence' in Cambodia, leaving mainly logistical and support staff; the Khmer Rouge filled the gap.

region.text: border zones of South Vietnam that Cliopatria adds to its 1973 DRV shape (51 cells), including Quang Tri around Cam Lo, the PRG's capital 1973-1975

ledger.note: 1973: the Paris Peace Accords (27 January) leave the PRG and the PAVN in their zones. The page is silent on the extent: the region is the difference between Cliopatria's 1972 and 1973 DRV shapes inside Vietnam, held by the Provisional Revolutionary Government, which 'signed the 1973 Paris Peace Treaty as an independent entity'. Reviewer follow-up, Paris Peace Accords page: it gives no extent for the PRG or PAVN zones ('North Vietnamese troops (PAVN) were allowed to remain in the South'; 'the communists enlarging the area under their control by the end of 1973'; the accords call for 'The withdrawal of all foreign troops from Laos and Cambodia'), so the zone stays Cliopatria's difference at confidence 1.

region.text: South Vietnam and the PRG zones, 'swiftly overrun'; the war 'ended on 30 April 1975'

ledger.note: 1975: Saigon falls (30 April). The PRG 'formally replaced the Republic of Vietnam' as the nominal government and, with the army of the North, 'governed South Vietnam for the next year', seen as a satellite of Hanoi; the page gives no date for the Spring Offensive. [Reviewer se-04-a 2026-10-19: confidence lowered from 3 to 2: the North Vietnam page says the Provisional Revolutionary Government 'alongside the North Vietnamese Army, governed South Vietnam for the next year' and the PRG page that it 'formally replaced the Republic of Vietnam to become the nominal and representative government of South Vietnam', so the DRV holding the land in 1975-76 is a reading, not the page's words; once a PRG dossier exists this should become the PRG's gain with a DRV vassal_start.]

region.text: border zones of South Vietnam that Cliopatria adds to its 1973 DRV shape (51 cells), including Quang Tri around Cam Lo, the PRG's capital 1973-1975

ledger.note: 1975: the zones merge into the conquest of South Vietnam (30 April, below).

region.text: the south-eastern border strip (Xekong, Attapu, eastern Savannakhet, Saravan; about 10,600 km2) that Cliopatria cuts from the Kingdom's shape in 1967: 'North Vietnam invaded and occupied parts of Laos as a supply route'

ledger.note: 1975: the strip passes to the Pathet Lao state with the end of the Kingdom of Laos: Pathet Lao forces took Vientiane on 23 August 1975 and the Lao People's Democratic Republic was proclaimed on 2 December 1975.

region.text: Attapeu, seized on 1 May 1970 by PAVN units joined with the Pathet Lao

ledger.note: 2 December 1975: the Laotian Civil War 'was officially declared over' and the Lao People's Democratic Republic was proclaimed, so Attapeu passes to the Pathet Lao state; mirrors kingdom-of-laos /ledger/11.

region.text: the Bolaven Plateau, captured in 1971 by Pathet Lao and PAVN forces; the 60 km circle is the researcher's reading

ledger.note: 2 December 1975: the Laotian Civil War 'was officially declared over' and the Lao People's Democratic Republic was proclaimed, so the Bolaven Plateau passes to the Pathet Lao state; mirrors kingdom-of-laos /ledger/12.

region.text: all Vietnam: 'officially reunited on 2 July 1976 as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam'

ledger.note: 1976: North and South unite as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam (2 July); the PRG page: the two 'constitutionally merged to form the current Socialist Republic of Vietnam'.

wars.outcome: The 1973 Paris Peace Accords (27 January) let the US and its allies withdraw 'By 1973'; the war 'ended on 30 April 1975' with South Vietnam overrun; reunification on 2 July 1976.
wars.note: The first year 1956 is the first Cliopatria year of the DRV, not the page's start of the war (the page was read for its end). Fronts by province are not on the pages opened.

certainty.note: Nominal claims and guerrilla fronts: the DRV's real hold is the mountain base and 'most rural areas'; the line north of the 16th parallel was an occupation boundary.
The 17th parallel set by the Geneva Accords, 'provisionally'; the page names no Ben Hai River or DMZ.
The border zones of 1973-1975 were held by the Provisional Revolutionary Government and the PAVN with no agreed lines.

notes: Wikidata Q172640 is shared with the Republic of Vietnam (South Vietnam, another part of this group); the two are different states (separate Wikipedia articles, North Vietnam and South Vietnam; opposing governments), so no merge here. The state begins on 2 September 1945, eleven years before Cliopatria's first DRV shape, and ends on 2 July 1976, a year after its last. Page budget (1-2) was spent on the North Vietnam article and the PRG article (the Cambodian campaign, Khmer Republic and Laotian Civil War pages, opened for the neighbouring dossiers, are cited for three occupation events); the 1973 shape is unverified beyond the PRG's capital at Cam Lo: it adds the PRG and PAVN border zones (51 cells in Vietnam, 37 in Laos, 14 in Cambodia) to the DRV and should be split into a PRG dossier (slug provisional-revolutionary-government-of-the-republic-of-south-vietnam; Cliopatria lacks it; formed 8 June 1969; capitals Tay Ninh 1969-72, Loc Ninh 1972-73, Cam Lo 1973-75, Saigon 1975-76). The Viet Minh's Viet Bac liberated zones and the Vietnam War's contested provinces year by year are not on the pages and are left to the group's additions batch. Cliopatria's Socialist Republic of Vietnam row begins in January 1976; the formal union is 2 July 1976. The 'republic-of-china' counterpart stands for the Chinese Nationalist occupation of the north (1945-46). Review fixes (2026-10-19): Attapu (1970-05) and the Bolaven Plateau (1971) occupations of Laos, with their 1975-12 ends, are added as mirrors of kingdom-of-laos /ledger/6, 7, 11 and 12 (Laotian Civil War page). The Chinese occupation of the north now starts in August 1945 on the August Revolution page ('starting August 1945'; no arrival day). The Ho Chi Minh trail page does not date the occupation of the 1967 strip as a whole (Tchepone May 1958, trail after July 1959, Attapeu and Salavan 1970), so 1967 stays Cliopatria's year at confidence 1 and is flagged for both dossiers. The Paris Peace Accords page gives no extent for the PRG and PAVN zones, so /ledger/9 stays at confidence 1. The 1975-04 gain of South Vietnam is at confidence 2 (reviewer); it becomes the PRG's gain plus a DRV vassal_start once a provisional-revolutionary-government-of-the-republic-of-south-vietnam dossier exists (none yet). Three more pages were opened on the reviewer's instruction, beyond the 1-2 page budget.
